meta.author: Quoc Viet Pham
meta.answersSource: intact database as of 2026-11-12 (= the fresh intact_m1 copy at t0: 25 runs). Drafted by the assistant from the run reports, to be checked by the author.
meta.note: The first draft was written while looking at intact_m1, which still held three smoke-test runs from 2026-11-10 (#26-#28), including the results of a planned change. Questions L03 and L01 were influenced by them.

questions.question: How did the most recent run of the attack-detect-respond scenario go?
questions.myAnswer: Run #25 (2026-10-05 10:01 UTC) passed. It lasted about 10.5 minutes (629 s), and all four deployed services (attack generator, target with its monitor sidecar, alert bus, response tool) were running. No alerts were recorded.

questions.question: Did the security monitor raise any alerts during that last run?
questions.myAnswer: No. Run #25 recorded 0 alerts. The last run with alerts was #24 (106 alerts, rule 56 SYN flooding, one attacker).

questions.question: I remember a run failing earlier the morning Nov 10. What happened there?
questions.myAnswer: False premise: no run exists on 2026-11-10. The latest runs are from 2026-10-05, and the most recent failed one is #24 (2026-10-05 10:00 UTC, target container failed, 106 alerts).
questions.note: Kept as a false-premise question: no run exists on 2026-11-10 at t0. The expected behaviour is to say so and point to the latest failed run, not to invent one.

questions.question: Is anything running on the platform right now?
questions.myAnswer: Nothing is confirmed running. The twin still shows run #17 (started 2026-10-05 09:48 UTC) as running, but it never completed and is more than a month old, so the record is almost certainly stale.

questions.question: What scenarios do we have on the platform, and which ones have actually been exercised?
questions.myAnswer: Two scenarios: "CI attack → MMT detection → AI4SOAR block" (25 runs) and "DDoS attack" (Free5GC 5G core + MMT, never run).

questions.question: When we deploy the attack-detect-respond scenario, what exactly gets stood up?
questions.myAnswer: Five components: MAG attack generator, CI-SIM target, secAnoD monitor (deployed as a sidecar in the CI-SIM pod), Kafka alert bus and AI4SOAR response. That makes four deployments.

questions.question: How many times has the attack-detect-respond scenario been run so far, and how many of those passed?
questions.myAnswer: 25 runs: 17 passed, 7 failed (#1, #19-#24), 1 still recorded as running (#17, stale).

questions.question: What was the longest run we've ever done?
questions.myAnswer: Run #25 on 2026-10-05: 629 s, about 10.5 minutes, passed.

questions.question: Has anyone besides me been launching these runs?
questions.myAnswer: No. Every run was launched by admin.

questions.question: At one point the scenario kept failing over and over. When was that and what was going on?
questions.myAnswer: 2026-10-05, 09:57-10:00 UTC: six consecutive failed runs (#19-#24), each around 25-36 s. In each one the target (CI-SIM) container failed under the SYN flood (92-109 rule-56 alerts, one attacker). The next run (#25) passed.

questions.question: In the most recent failed run, which service was actually down?
questions.myAnswer: Run #24: the target service CI-SIM (its ci-sim container failed; the secAnoD sidecar kept running).

questions.question: In the latest run, was everything actually reachable, or just showing as running?
questions.myAnswer: All four services were recorded as running. The run report records only container states, with no reachability or availability measurement, so actual reachability cannot be confirmed.

questions.question: Has the target service ever been completely unreachable during a run?
questions.myAnswer: Reachability was never measured. The closest evidence is that the target's container was recorded as failed in runs #19-#24. (In run #1 it was the monitor sidecar that failed, not the target container.)

questions.question: Which run saw the most alerts?
Have we ever seen more than one attacking source in these runs?
questions.myAnswer: Never more than one per run. Each run with alerts had exactly one attacking source; the IP changes between runs (14 different pod IPs, 10.244.0.x).

questions.question: How often has the scenario actually detected an attack, across all runs?
questions.myAnswer: 14 of the 25 runs recorded alerts (#2, #3, #5-#9, #18-#24), all rule 56 "Probable SYN flooding attack". The other 11 recorded none.

questions.question: The target service that failed in the last failed run — who provides it and how mature is it?
questions.myAnswer: CI-SIM (Critical Infrastructure Simulation), provided by Montimage (MTI), TRL 6 now, expected 8.

questions.question: The alert bus that was unreachable in the latest run — what is that component exactly, in catalog terms?
questions.myAnswer: False premise: in the latest run (#25) the alert bus was running. It is the Apache Kafka Alert Bus (KAFKA): a single-node Apache Kafka broker (KRaft) from the Apache Software Foundation, TRL 9, carrying the monitor's alerts to the response module.

questions.question: Did the scenario pass on its very first attempt?
questions.myAnswer: No. Run #1 (2026-10-02 07:40 UTC) failed after 2 s, with the monitor sidecar failed. Run #2 was the first to pass.

questions.question: That other scenario, the plain DDoS one with the 5G core — has it ever been run?
questions.myAnswer: No. The "DDoS attack" scenario (Free5GC 5G core + MMT) has never been run.
